plain_what: Gives every word in the vocabulary a unique, fixed starting address built from its prime number (2, 3, 5, ...) and the phases of the Riemann zeta zeros. It is computed once, offline, and stored as a plain table of small integers. It replaces the random starting vectors, which had only 16 distinct values for 4,096 words.
how_it_works: Token v gets prime p = p_(id(v)+1), so the vocabulary maps one-to-one onto the first V primes (p_4096 = 38873). For each of the first 512 pinned zeta-zero ordinates gamma_k the phase is theta_k(p) = gamma_k * ln(p) mod 2*pi, the unit phasor z_k = cos(theta_k) + i sin(theta_k). Four consecutive channels per 8-D block form a vector in C^4, split into two C^2->R^4 spinor pairs, quantized to integers (PhaseQ29, UnitS3Q30), and embedded in the four orthogonal 2-D root planes of the 16-root E8 orbit. Each block takes the orbit root with the largest exact integer inner product. The writer cell of a token is the pair (root of block 0, root of last block), a 16 x 16 = 256 cell grid. A quota pass puts exactly V/256 = 16 tokens in each cell, and a uniqueness pass gives interior blocks distinct roots so all 4,096 full vectors differ. Floating point (ln, sin, cos) is confined to this one-time host step (D32 Oct 14 exception). The output is an integer table loaded as Snapshot.table by Device::from_snapshot, and every word is admitted as a root on the GPU. Two matched nulls share the same pipeline: TangentNull shifts every gamma_k by 1.0, NormalNull permutes the primes and distorts off the critical line.
geometry: Primes (prime-rank bijection), Riemann zeta-zero ordinates on the critical line (phasors), C^4->R^4 and C^8->R^8 realification, unit quaternions on S^3 (Q30), the 16-root E8 orbit and its four orthogonal 2-D root planes, 16 x 16 writer cell grid. Fixed-width integer table; no learned parameters.

status_reason: The qualified constructor and the pinned_table_v1 loader are on the current M1 path: PrimeZeta is the P8 baseline and the zero-mass fallback inside the A8 table. Trained attribution against the two nulls is NOT_RUN and held. Injectivity comes from the quota and uniqueness pass shared with both nulls, not from prime phases (docs/labs/prime-zeta-construction-2026-10-14/README.md).

rule_compat.D11: Compatible. The served artifact sees only an integer table (i32 root coordinates); no float and no multiplier at serving. All float work happens once, offline, on the host.
rule_compat.D23: No softmax, sigmoid, tanh or other squashing anywhere in the construction. sin and cos are used only to build phasors.
rule_compat.D30: No GEMM or dense matmul. Construction scores each token with a few exact 8-element integer inner products against 16 roots, once, on the host; the model only does table reads.
rule_compat.D32_D37: Float is confined to the D32 October 14 complex-plane zeta-zero exception (gamma_k ln p, the phasors and the C^4->R^4 / C^8->R^8 maps), which D37 item 4 keeps as a separate rule. Everything downstream is integer, and admit_ptx found 0 float instructions in the 11-entry PTX.

figure_ideas: A prime ladder (2, 3, 5, 7, ... on a log axis) feeding eight small clock dials, one per zeta zero. As you slide a token's prime up, each dial's hand rotates by gamma_k times ln p. An arrow then drops the token onto a 16 x 16 board of writer cells and the dot jumps to its cell, with 16 dots stacking up in each cell. (Static art already exists at docs/figures/geometry/zeta-phases.svg and prime-addressing.svg to animate.)

Before and after for 4,096 tokens drawn as dots. Left (default xorshift): the dots collapse into 16 piles of 256 and a caption shows that ties go to the lowest token id, so only one dot per pile can ever win. Right (PrimeZeta): 256 cells with 16 dots each, every dot distinct. A counter animates 16 -> 4,096 distinct vectors and 1,986 -> 14,287 reachable DEV rows.

Three-panel control comparison: the same ten tokens placed by PrimeZeta, TangentNull (all gamma shifted by 1.0) and NormalNull (primes shuffled). Lines connect each token's cell across panels to show that 4,090 to 4,096 of 4,096 tokens move, so the nulls are genuinely different tables.
